problems: WATERMARK CONFLICT: the assignment text said high 95% / low 85%, but the normative spec says 85% / 75% in three places: memory-and-paging.md §3.1 and KMM-05 (test title 'MEM-06 background reclaim starts above 85% and stops at 75%'), syscall-abi.md §4.4.5, and kernel/src/core/README.md. I implemented the spec values; they live in params.ts as highWm/lowWm and can be overridden.

WIRE-CONTRACT CONFLICT for /api/swap: memory-and-paging.md §4.5 specifies headers Plt-Sha256 (over the uncompressed BODY) and Plt-Size, plus a reply of 201 {sha256,size,gen}. backend-api.md §3.11, which owns the server side, specifies X-Plotinium-Checksum (over the uncompressed bytes uploaded), X-Plotinium-Raw-Size and X-Plotinium-Encoding, plus a reply of 200 {stored,checksum}. I followed backend-api.md: the checksum covers the uncompressed page file (header + body), because that is what a streaming server tee can verify. I also send ?gen= and X-Plotinium-Gen. The client accepts 200 or 201 and either `checksum` or `sha256` in the reply. Header names are one constant, SWAP_HEADERS in remote.ts. The page body is still verified against the PTE hash on every page-in.

PROTOCOL SHAPE MISMATCH: protocol/src/sys/mem.ts has MemAllocArgs {bytes, key?, kind?: 'state'|'buffer'} → {segId, bytes}. The memory spec has {kind: 'logical'|'chunk'|'segment', size, label} → {pageIds}. The kernel API (MemoryManager.alloc) follows the memory spec, so the dispatcher handler must map between the two. Details are in integration_notes.

dsa/lru and dsa/heap are IMPLEMENTED=false (C16). MemoryManager's default factories use LruCache and BinaryHeap, which throw NotImplementedError, so the memory manager cannot run in production until R1 implements them. All tests inject test-only doubles from kernel/src/core/mm/fixtures/doubles.ts. lru.test.ts also runs against the real LruCache automatically once the flag flips.

The dsa/lru interface has no sentinel segments, although memory-and-paging.md §3.5.1 describes them. The pager therefore uses three LRU instances (HOT, COLD, SPEC); every operation is still a constant number of O(1) dsa/lru calls. Speculative pages use putAtLru, as DSA-LRU-02 requires.

Real bugs found and fixed while testing: (1) a lost wake-up in the reclaim loop: a synchronous drop of a kernel-held page freed memory before it was counted as 'freeing', and the restart request arrived while the loop was still marked running; (2) charge leaks when a process exited during a page-in, prefetch or fault await; (3) the IndexedDB back end left an unverified record behind after a failed write. For (3), note that an IndexedDB put replaces the previous generation, so no older copy survives a failed write. That is safe because only dirty pages are rewritten, and their old local copy is already marked 'stale'.

Design decision beyond the spec: reclaim does not suspend a process whose own mem reservation is currently blocked. Its state page is deferred to the end of the reclaim pass, because re-issuing a pending mem.alloc after a page-in is not modelled. An explicit mem.pageOut of such a process answers EBUSY.

Browser APIs (OPFS sync access handles, IndexedDB, CompressionStream in a real worker) were exercised only through in-memory fakes that implement the same structural interfaces. The real-browser MEM-03/MEM-05 tests, the MEM-04 new-profile end-to-end test and the calibration job still need Playwright on the lab machine.
mm.ts is large (about 2,070 lines after formatting), because the page-I/O orchestration shares a lot of private state. It could later be split into a pager module and a reclaim module.

integration_notes:
HOST WIRING (kernel/src/host, not my path):
(1) Spawn blkio as a nested module worker: new Worker(new URL('../blkio/blkio.worker.ts', import.meta.url), {type:'module'}). Then `const dev = await BlkioClient.connect(worker)`; the Worker satisfies BlkioEndpoint. Log dev.fallback to bootlog when it is set.
(2) Build the remote tier: `const remote = new HttpRemoteSwap({ fetch: (u, i) => fetch(u, i), gzip: streamGzip, digestHex: subtleSha256Hex })`, importing from '@plotinium/kernel' blkio and core/mm.
(3) `const mm = new MemoryManager({ clock: {now: () => performance.now(), schedule: (ms, fn) => { const t = setTimeout(fn, ms); return () => clearTimeout(t); }}, executor: <MemExecutorPort adapter over the §4.3 frames>, device: dev, remote, backing: <ai_vecseg reader>, hooks: {setWaiting → PCB.waitingOn, suspended/resumed → PROC-06 transitions, restoring/restored → compositor 'restoring {wid,doneBytes,totalBytes}' messages (map pid→wids), event → event bus mem.fault/mem.evict/mem.pressure, klog → klog ring, notice → desktop notification}, kernelStructures: () => [{name:'tree',entries,bytesPerEntry}, ...], localCap: dev.capBytes, calibration: loadCalibration(calibrationJson).constants })`.
(4) Call mm.tick() every 1 s.
(5) At the mm service start (boot stage 4), run mm.sweep(keep) with the (uid, osSession) pairs referenced by os_sessions layouts.

KERNEL LIFECYCLE CALLS:
- spawn: mm.register(pid, {uid, app, label, osSession, checkpointable, special, window, softLimit, pinnedService: manifest.pinned}) and then await mm.admit(pid, {initialStateBytes, heavy: manifest.heavy, prio: effPrio}). admit rejects EAGAIN 'thrashing' for heavy spawns while the thrashing guard is on.
- reap or kill: mm.exit(pid).
- Every slice-end frame: mm.onSlice(pid, touched, dirtied).
- At yield points: `const w = mm.measureState(pid, encodedBytes); if (w) block on it`.
- Compositor events: minimised → mm.setMinimised(pid, true); restored → await mm.restoreWindow(pid) BEFORE focus is delivered; focused → mm.setFocus([pid, ...foreground TTY group]).
- Non-pre-emptive kernel sections: mm.setNpSection(pid, on).
- Non-restartable call in flight: mm.setNonRestartable(pid, on).
- ai.search focus: mm.setSearchPin(pid, pageIds, on).
- ai.embed: register with special:true and checkpointable:false, `await mm.declareWorkerPage(pid, measuredBytes)` BEFORE spawning the worker, and implement terminateWorker/respawnWorker on the executor port.
- syncd LIVE state: mm.setOnline(live, uidsTheAuthSessionCanActAs).
- Checkpoints: mm.checkpoint(pid) for visibilitychange→hidden, for BOOT-12 before SIGTERM, and for idle checkpoints. After each window-process checkpoint, write mm.pageMap(pid) into os_sessions.window_layout[].proc.
- Restore in a new session: mm.register(newPid, ...), then mm.adoptPageMap(newPid, entry.proc), then `await mm.pageIn(newPid, {from:'session'})`.

SYSCALL DISPATCHER (mem.* handlers):
- mem.alloc → mm.alloc(pid, {kind, size, label, prio}). Map protocol kind 'buffer' → 'chunk', and the default/'state' → 'logical'. The protocol returns {segId, bytes} but the kernel returns {pageIds}: either change the protocol (below) or keep a segId → pageIds map in the handler.
- mem.declare → mm.declare(pid, key, bytes). mem.free {key} → mm.undeclare(pid, key); mem.free {segId} → mm.free(pid, pageIds).
- mem.stat → mm.memStat({pid, callerUid}), which returns the protocol MemStat shape.
- mem.prefetch {pid, pages} → mm.prefetch(pid, pages). mem.hint → mm.setHint(app, ttlMs).
- Errors are MmError {errno, reason}; the reasons used are 'exceeds-budget', 'mem-pressure', 'thrashing', 'no-free-memory', 'checksum', 'storage', 'killed', 'unknown-segment' and 'codec'.
- Sysctl keys: mm.budget → mm.setBudget(bytes) (range 64 MiB…2 GiB); mm.softLimit → mm.setSoftLimit(bytes); mm.swap.tier → mm.setTier('auto'|'local'|'remote').

REQUESTED PROTOCOL CHANGES (TODO(protocol), not made by me):
(a) Register the calls mem.fault, mem.setBacking, mem.undeclare, mem.pageOut, mem.pageIn and mem.swapctl (memory-and-paging §4.2).
(b) Align MemAllocArgs/Ret with the page model: kind 'logical'|'chunk'|'segment', size, label → pageIds.
(c) Add protocol/src/host/executor-mem.ts with MemKernelToExec and MemExecToKernel (§4.3); the kernel side is MemExecutorPort, ExecPage and CheckpointResult in mm.ts.
(d) Add protocol/src/session/layout.ts WindowLayoutEntry.proc (§3.12.2), mirrored by ProcPageMap and PageMapEntry in mm.ts.
(e) Move the KlogMem record type from core/mm/types.ts to the protocol or klog types.
(f) Register the EAGAIN reason 'mem-pressure' and the EINVAL reason 'codec' in REGISTERED_REASONS, and ENOMEM if it is approved.
(g) Add result shapes so apps/coreutils can format free, vmstat -p and pmap: FreeReport, VmCounters, VmstatProcRow and PmapReport in core/mm/stats.ts. The current MemStat has no page rows and no cumulative paging counters.

KERNEL PACKAGE ENTRY (kernel/src/index.ts, owned by another agent): please add `export * from './core/mm/index.ts'` and `export * from './blkio/index.ts'`, or a './mm' subpath export in kernel/package.json.

SERVER (/api/swap): the client sends PUT /api/swap/{osSession}/{pid}/{pageId}?gen=g with a gzip body and the headers X-Plotinium-Checksum (hex SHA-256 of the UNCOMPRESSED page file, header + body), X-Plotinium-Raw-Size, X-Plotinium-Encoding: gzip and X-Plotinium-Gen. It expects 200 or 201 with {checksum} (or {sha256}) equal to what it sent, 429 with {retryAfterMs} or a Retry-After header, and 401 to pause. GET on the same path must return the gzip stream with X-Plotinium-Raw-Size and X-Plotinium-Encoding; 403 maps to EACCES and 404 to ENOENT. DELETE applies to a page or a session. The header names are one constant, SWAP_HEADERS in core/mm/remote.ts, if the server chooses differently.

VITEST: kernel/src/core/mm/fixtures and kernel/src/blkio/fixtures are test support; the repo coverage config already excludes **/fixtures/**. The 2x stress test has a 60 s timeout and the thrashing test a 30 s timeout. Every other test runs in under 1 s. No config change is needed.
